best_idea: A road tile's shape is a 4-bit neighbour mask looked up in a 16-entry table, and every road edit re-derives the edited tile and its four neighbours; a 3x3 building is stamped as nine base-plus-offset tiles.
decision_why: Zones are data, so the grid stores tile kinds and the client derives shapes; no zone file carries sprite ids. Adapt means our own tile sheet, one neighbour rule for all four directions, and a lot score that counts roads only (the donor's lot test also counts water, trees and other tiles up to id 206).
acceptance: A player lays a road beside an existing road and it joins on the same frame; a T-junction shows the T piece; a house goes on the free 3x3 block that touches the most roads. A test asserts that after each placeRoad every road tile's shape equals shapeFor(mask of its four neighbours) and a stamped block holds nine distinct ids base..base+8.
